title: 2022 building code energy and accessibility standards adopted (Tasmania)
summary: Tasmania applied the NCC 2022 commercial energy efficiency and condensation provisions from 1 October 2023 and livable housing from 1 October 2024, and did not adopt the housing and apartment energy efficiency provisions.

instruments.title: National Construction Code 2022
instruments.provisions: energy efficiency, condensation management and livable housing design provisions (Volumes One and Two, the ABCB Housing Provisions and the Livable Housing Design Standard)

instruments.title: Building Act 2016 (Tas)
instruments.provisions: s 4(1), definition of National Construction Code

commenced.what: NCC 2022 adopted as a whole; its energy efficiency, condensation management and livable housing provisions started later (the dates below)
Commercial energy efficiency and condensation management provisions applied
Livable housing design provisions applied; housing and apartment energy efficiency not adopted

direction_rationale: The 2022 code raised minimum energy performance for new homes to 7 stars and added livable housing design requirements. Design and compliance costs are partly fixed per dwelling and may fall hardest on small builders, lowering entry and raising exit.
comparison: Staggered and partial adoption, October 2023 to May 2025 (NSW and WA did not adopt livable housing; Tasmania did not adopt housing energy efficiency; the NT kept 5 stars)

verified.notes: Dates by provision area from the ABCB adoption-dates table (correct as at 22 September 2023; data/processed/ncc/adoption_2022.csv); the whole-edition date from the 'History of adoption' table in the NCC 2025 dataset (version 1.2). Adopting laws are those the state's schedule in NCC 2025 names (data/processed/ncc/regulatory_map.json).

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use. Revised on 27 November 2026 from the ABCB's NCC datasets and adoption pages (docs/plan_ncc_ingestion.md, phase N2; DECISIONS E-501): commencements by provision area, the adopting laws, and the 2025 pause.

assessment.summary: Adopts the 2022 National Construction Code's higher energy efficiency (7-star) and livable housing standards for new homes. Tasmania adopted livable housing but not the energy efficiency provisions. The standards cut running costs and improve access, which are not weighed here; they also add to the cost of building.

marks.reason: Adds design and compliance costs to every new home, which weigh most on small builders.
Adopting only part of the national code, or a local version, leaves builders working across states with different rules.

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission estimates housing construction regulation costs about 1% of GDP a year.

responsible.note: Produces the National Construction Code that each jurisdiction adopts.

history.what: The Australian Government announced a pause on further residential changes to the NCC until mid-2029, after NCC 2025, except essential safety and quality changes, keeping the 2022 residential standards, including 7-star energy efficiency.
